title: The small detail
prompt: You have time for one closer look before moving on. What would you rather leave knowing?
intro: Come and have a look at this one. You can turn it round, too.

choices.text: How they worked out what this animal was.
choices.evidence: Chose the evidence behind an identification.

choices.text: What survived from the original, and what was restored.
choices.evidence: Wanted to distinguish retained material from later changes.

choices.text: What I could notice before reading the explanation.
choices.evidence: Chose space for a first-hand impression.

choices.text: What different people noticed when they first saw it.
choices.evidence: Wanted multiple perspectives on the same object.

title: The missing piece
prompt: This skeleton is missing a piece. Which version would you rather encounter in the museum?
intro: There’s a bit missing from this one. We’ve checked under the cabinet.

choices.text: Show two possible reconstructions beside the gap. I want to compare them.
choices.evidence: Preferred competing explanations to a single reconstruction.

choices.text: Leave the gap visible. I want to see exactly what remains.
choices.evidence: Kept absence visible rather than filling it in.

choices.text: Add a removable reconstruction. I want to try seeing the whole animal.
choices.evidence: Chose a reversible way to move forward with incomplete information.

choices.text: Let visitors switch between versions. Different views may help different people.
choices.evidence: Made room for different ways of understanding the exhibit.

title: What gets remembered
prompt: You’re making a small record of an ordinary day, to be opened years from now. What would you put at its centre?
intro: These are things people left behind. Footprints, mostly. What would you leave to remember a day by?

choices.text: The unanswered question I kept returning to.
choices.evidence: Kept an unresolved question as the day's central record.

choices.text: A small routine I might otherwise forget.
choices.evidence: Preserved an easily overlooked part of everyday life.

choices.text: A decision that changed how the day went.
choices.evidence: Focused on a moment of making a difference.

choices.text: An exchange with someone that stayed with me.
choices.evidence: Remembered the day through an interaction.

title: The surprise drawer
prompt: You set aside an afternoon for something familiar. Just as you begin, an unexpected invitation arrives. Both sound good. What do you do?
intro: Go on, open it. I think this is the right drawer.

choices.text: Get a little more detail before deciding which interests me more.
choices.evidence: Sought more context before choosing.

choices.text: Keep the afternoon I planned; suggest another day for the invitation.
choices.evidence: Protected an existing intention while leaving a future opening.

choices.text: Take the invitation. I can return to my original plan.
choices.evidence: Accepted an opportunity while treating the original plan as recoverable.

choices.text: See whether we can combine some of both without making it awkward.
choices.evidence: Looked for a workable shared arrangement.

title: The next test
prompt: An unfamiliar specimen could be studied in several ways. There is funding for one next step. Which would you back?
intro: We’ve got enough money to try one of these. Just one, though. Have a look and see what you think.

choices.text: A detailed scan: more information, but it may not settle the main question.
choices.evidence: Accepted an incomplete answer in exchange for more evidence.

choices.text: Better storage first: protect the specimen, though the answer will wait.
choices.evidence: Protected future options before pursuing an immediate answer.

choices.text: A tiny sample test: a clearer answer, but it permanently uses some material.
choices.evidence: Accepted a stated cost for a more decisive next step.

choices.text: A joint study with another museum: shared expertise, but a slower start.
choices.evidence: Chose shared expertise despite a coordination cost.

title: Same label, different view
prompt: You and someone else come away from the same experience with different impressions. What would you most want to do?
intro: Same display, two different descriptions. Hmm. Have a look at both.

choices.text: Compare the particular details each of us noticed.
choices.evidence: Explored the observations behind different impressions.

choices.text: Keep both accounts intact; neither needs replacing yet.
choices.evidence: Preserved separate accounts without forcing resolution.

choices.text: Try a different approach together and see what happens next.
choices.evidence: Used another experience to move beyond the disagreement.

choices.text: Find out why that impression mattered to them.
choices.evidence: Prioritised the personal significance of another perspective.

title: Room to change
prompt: A place you love is being changed. The proposal has real benefits, but it will feel different. What would you speak up for first?
intro: Here’s the old layout, and here’s the new one. Take a look. What do you think?

choices.text: A clear account of what the change is meant to improve.
choices.evidence: Asked for the purpose and evidence behind a change.

choices.text: Keeping one part that makes the place feel like itself.
choices.evidence: Protected a specific source of continuity.

choices.text: A trial period so we can experience it before deciding.
choices.evidence: Favoured a practical, reversible trial.

choices.text: A way for the people who use it to shape the proposal.
choices.evidence: Prioritised participation by the people affected.

title: The shared field kit
prompt: A small group has an afternoon to explore somewhere unfamiliar. The basics are covered. What extra would you most want to bring?
intro: Everything we need is packed! There’s a little space left. Anything you’d like to bring?

choices.text: A field guide, so we can make sense of what we find.
choices.evidence: Brought a resource for interpreting discoveries together.

choices.text: A notebook, so details don't disappear when the day ends.
choices.evidence: Made room to retain details beyond the moment.

choices.text: A map with a few optional detours marked.
choices.evidence: Kept room for self-directed exploration within a usable plan.

choices.text: A shared camera, so everyone can add what caught their eye.
choices.evidence: Chose a shared record that others could shape.
